summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 17.3 to Angular 18.2 with `ng update @angular/core@18 @angular/cli@18`, whose migration replaced the deprecated `HttpClientModule` with `provideHttpClient(withInterceptorsFromDi())` in app.module.ts. The hop file listed no related packages, but @ngrx/* 17 pins `@angular/core@^17.0.0`, so a clean `npm install` failed on peer resolution until @ngrx was bumped to 18.1.1 via `ng update @ngrx/store@18`; that migration also rewrote the reducer's removed `TypedAction` import to `Action`. `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` pass; `npm run test` still fails for the same pre-existing reason as at baseline.
changes: src/app/app.module.ts: the Angular 18 migration dropped the deprecated `HttpClientModule` import and added `providers: [provideHttpClient(withInterceptorsFromDi())]`, preserving the existing DI-registered HTTP_INTERCEPTORS behaviour. The migration also collapsed the whole @NgModule decorator onto fewer lines; reindented by hand back to the original layout so the diff shows only the real change.

@ngrx/{store,effects,entity,router-store,store-devtools} ^17.2.0 -> ^18.1.1 via `ng update @ngrx/store@18`. Not listed in the hop file, but required: NgRx 17 declares a peer of @angular/core ^17.0.0, so `npm install` aborted with ERESOLVE against Angular 18.

src/app/state/reducers/employee.reducer.ts: NgRx v18 removed `TypedAction`, so its migration switched `Action` to come from the public `@ngrx/store` entrypoint instead of the deep `@ngrx/store/src/models` path. The migration left both the new and the old import line in place (a duplicate-identifier error); removed the stale deep-import line by hand.
Removed `@ngrx/operators`, which the NgRx v18 `concatLatestFrom` migration added unconditionally: `concatLatestFrom` is not used anywhere in src/, so the dependency was dead weight.

Declined the optional `use-application-builder` CLI migration, keeping the existing `@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` builder and the aspnet-prerendering SSR setup, per the smallest-correct-change rule.
package-lock.json regenerated by npm; verified with a from-scratch `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps or --force needed).
manual_followups: Tests still fail exactly as at baseline and for the same reason: the `test` target in angular.json lists the stylesheet as "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so Karma reports "Can't resolve 'styles.css'" and aborts before running any spec. Fixing that one path would let the suite run; left alone here because the hop rules only require that a baseline failure not get worse.
rxjs is still ^6.6.7. Angular 18 accepts it (peer is ^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0), but rxjs 6 is end-of-life and Angular 19 narrows the range, so the rxjs 7 bump should happen in the next hop or two.

The app remains NgModule-based on the deprecated `browser` builder with `BrowserModule.withServerTransition` and aspnet-prerendering SSR. Angular 19+ pushes harder on the application builder and standalone APIs, so this migration is still pending and will likely become mandatory in a later hop.

Deprecated/legacy devDeps remain unchanged (tslint, codelyzer, protractor, node-sass, core-js 2, @types/node 12, jasmine 3.10). None are exercised by the required checks, but they block a move to ESLint and will eventually conflict with newer Node/Angular.
